questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.id_repeat: Could you tell me that once more?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match what we have.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't continue with this call. Please call us on the number on your card.

lines.ask_today_multi: Could you pay the full amount today?

lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below the lowest amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed.
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. Could you pay on {date} instead?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day could you pay {amount}?

lines.dispute_line: I understand, thank you for telling me.

lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our payment plans team.

lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?

assumptions: The brief uses the call variables full_name and salutation, not first_name, last_name and title. Lines use {full_name} and {salutation}, and both are declared in call_variables.
Currency is euros. get_account amounts are in euro cents, so amount_scale is 100. create_promise also takes cents (rule 18), so promise_scale is null.
Business days are Monday to Saturday (workdays 0-5). The holidays are 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25. 'The Nth business day after today' counts from tomorrow.
The brief does not define 'next <weekday>'. The default following_week is used (a week runs Monday to Sunday).

Callbacks: today or either of the next two business days, so days are today plus within_business_days:2, and business_days_only is true. Hours are 09:00-18:00 Monday to Friday and 09:00-13:00 Saturday, both ends included. There are no callbacks on Sunday (window null). A callback must be later than now.
Callback max_asks is 2: the first ask, then one proposed valid time (rule 4). If that is refused, the call closes as contact_failed/no_callback.
Identity: one wrong answer is forgiven over the whole check and the next ends it, so max_wrong is 2, counted over the whole check rather than per question.

Verify responses: 'correct' means the answer matched and 'identity_passed' means all three passed. The API has no 'wrong answers left' field and no hint field, so left and hint are empty and the engine counts wrong answers against max_wrong=2. A wrongly formatted answer returns ok=false and is not counted.

Answer formats come from the API and rule 7. birth_year is four digits (kind year, so length is omitted as the spec format says). customer_code is five capital letters or digits with no spaces. birth_date is DD.MM.YYYY (%d.%m.%Y). A numbers-only date is read day, month, year.
The opening must say the call is recorded. It uses the active form 'We record this call.'

Floor: a card uses statement_minimum_cents. An overdraft uses 20% of amount_due_cents, rounded up to the next whole euro, and an amount already in whole euros is not raised (floor_pct 20, floor_round up_unit). floor_pct applies only to the overdraft, because the overdraft has no floor_field. Examples: 48735 cents -> 97.47 -> 98 euros (9800); 50000 cents -> exactly 100 euros, not raised. Credit and overdraft limits are never used.
The brief does not say what happens if the floor is above the amount due. The floor is capped at the full amount due.
get_account returns one product object under 'account', not a list. list_field is 'account', id_field is 'product_id', type_field is 'product_kind'.

Early band (1-15): the deadline is the last business day of next week. Saturday counts; if it is a holiday, the business day before it is used. Example: now Thu 2026-11-12, Sat 2026-11-21 is a holiday, so the deadline is Fri 2026-11-20. 1 attempt.
Middle band (16-40): the deadline depends on the product. Card is the 8th business day after today and overdraft the 5th, counting from tomorrow (deadline_by_type). 2 attempts.
Late band (41-60): the deadline is the later of the last business day of the current month and the 3rd business day after today. 2 attempts.

Recoveries (61 or more days overdue) is written as days_overdue outside every band, through bands_outside {event: recoveries}. Rule 22 needs no proposal and no promise, even one the customer offers, which a band with attempts would not guarantee. The agent says recoveries_line, transfers to queue recoveries and closes handed_over/recoveries, with no note. A days_overdue below 1 cannot happen (the brief calls only customers who are late) and would follow the same route.

Rule 13: a Sunday or holiday on or before the deadline moves to the business day before it, or to the first business day after it if that day would be before today. deadline_adjust is previous_business_day.
Rule 14: refusing the deadline offered for a too-late date is a flat refusal (refuse_deadline_is_refusal true).
Rule 19: the first ask is the full amount today, in the exact words 'Could you pay the full amount today?'. It is not a persuasion attempt.

Ladder: attempt 1 is the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor on that day if the customer already said the full amount is too much. Attempt 2 (middle and late only) is the floor on the deadline. The early band uses only attempt 1. The last step is never repeated.

Too much: the single floor offer of rule 17 ('offer the floor once') is attempt 1, the floor on the 2nd business day after today (too_much_floor attempt_1), as rule 20's 'the floor on that day instead' says. A separate floor offer for today would mean offering the floor twice.
Below the floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. Refusing it is a flat refusal.
add_note is used only for system_fault (rule 24), paid_claim (26), disputed (27) and vulnerable (28). notes.enabled is false.

The add_note request has no product-id field: only customer_id, reason (required) and an optional free-text 'text' field. The engine needs an n_product slot, so it is mapped to 'text', and the product id is sent as the note's free text. No field was invented.

Hardship: one sentence of sympathy and no persuasion, then add_note vulnerable, transfer to care, and close handed_over/vulnerable. transfer_support carries the same values, including note vulnerable, so the note is written before the transfer on either path (rules 28 and 32).

Payment plan or lower repayments: transfer to payment_plans and close handed_over/restructure. Request for a person: ask once whether the agent can help, then transfer to customer_desk and close handed_over/agent_request.
If create_promise fails, it is retried once. A second failure leads to record_failed, add_note system_fault, and close no_commitment/system_error.
After ok:true the agent says 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' (sms_line) and closes as promised. The default single 'anything else' turn is kept.
The brief does not cover changing a promise that is already recorded, so promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
Saying twice that they do not want to talk closes as no_commitment/declined (max_not_talk 2).
If the answer to the confirm question is still unclear after asking twice, the call closes as contact_failed/unresolved.
When identity fails, the agent refers the customer to the number on their card, as rule 8 says.
